title: Verification, documentation and handover limits
audience: Coordinators, supervisors and trained workers who may be asked about, triage, refer or document cleaning and water-removal work after a flood or water event. Not a qualification or authority to enter a flood-affected building, energise its systems, or certify it as dry, safe or habitable.
learningOutcomes: Write a handover that separates cleaning completion, drying verification, hygienic release and occupancy clearance, and refuse to merge them.

instruction.heading: Scope and authority
instruction.body: This lesson teaches how to keep four separate claims apart in a handover: cleaning completion, drying verification, hygienic release and occupancy clearance. It does not issue any of them. Completing it does not give a licence, certificate or approval.

instruction.heading: Verification, documentation and handover limits
instruction.body: Cleaning completion, drying verification, hygienic release and building occupancy clearance are separate claims, and each has a different responsible professional. Create a defensible handover that records the work completed, the evidence, the outstanding defects, the referrals made and the customer's acknowledgement. Report actual observations and refer formal clearance to the qualified authority. Do not present the completion of cleaning as proof that the building is dry, hygienic or safe to occupy.

procedure: List the work completed and the evidence for each item.
List the outstanding defects, the referrals made and the tests still needed.
State cleaning completion as its own claim, with no statement about drying, hygiene or occupancy.
Refer drying verification, hygienic release and occupancy clearance to the responsible professionals, by name.
Record the customer's acknowledgement of the limits.
Refuse any request for a dry, hygienic or occupancy statement, and record the refusal.

workedExamples.situation: After the cleaning has finished, a customer asks for a certificate that the house is dry and safe to live in.
workedExamples.reasoning: Only the completed cleaning and the observed conditions. Drying verification, hygienic release and occupancy clearance are separate claims for different professionals. Record the referrals and do not issue the certificate.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaning company's handover template has one line: 'Site restored and safe.'
workedExamples.reasoning: Replace the line with the completed cleaning and the four separate claims, each with its responsible party. 'Restored and safe' is a claim the cleaning does not establish.

equipmentAndPpe: No PPE is issued for the paper handover.

commonErrors.error: Telling a customer that cleaning completion means the house is dry and safe.
commonErrors.prevention: Separate the four claims and refer each one.

commonErrors.error: Signing a handover that certifies dryness.

commonErrors.prevention: List every referral and its status.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: This lesson does not issue a dry, hygienic, structural or occupancy statement. Completing it does not give a licence, certificate or approval.
A cleaning completion, a drying reading or a visual inspection is not a clearance for hygienic release, structural safety, electrical safety or occupancy.

qualityStandard: The learner keeps the four claims separate.
The learner refuses any dry, hygienic or occupancy statement.
documentationEvidence: Completion handover: completed work, evidence, outstanding defects, referrals and the customer's acknowledgement.
summary: Refuse dry, hygienic and occupancy statements.

knowledgeChecks.question: A customer asks for a certificate that the house is dry and safe to live in after the cleaning. What can be written?
options: Only the completed cleaning and observed conditions, with drying, hygienic release and occupancy clearance referred to their responsible parties.
A certificate that the house is dry and safe to live in, since the cleaning was done properly and the team checked every room in the house
A certificate for the cleaned rooms that the owner can show to the insurer, so the claim can be closed quickly and the cleaning is accepted

knowledgeChecks.question: Which set lists the four claims that must not be merged in a handover?
options: Cleaning completion, drying verification, hygienic release and occupancy clearance
Cleaning completion, price and invoice date

moduleAuthority.heading: Module authority and restricted work
moduleAuthority.body: This module is training content. It does not grant authority to enter a flood-affected building, to carry out regulated flood restoration, to energise or isolate electrical, gas or solar systems, to remove sewage or contaminated water, to dispose of waste, or to certify that a property is dry, hygienic, structurally sound or safe to occupy. Completing this lesson does not give a licence, certificate or approval. Some of the work described is restricted to licensed, authorised or specially trained people, including electrical and gas work, structural assessment, sewage handling and some disposal. The site controller, the owner, the insurer and the competent professionals each hold separate decisions, and none of them replaces the others. Where the controlling authority or the competent professional is not identified, stop and refer.

stopWorkAndReferral.heading: Stop-work and referral rules for this module
stopWorkAndReferral.body: Stop and refer whenever any of these is true: permission to enter or written safety clearance is missing; the contamination is unknown; a structural hazard, a slip or a confined space has not been cleared; an electrical, gas or solar system is water-exposed or has not been licensed for re-energisation; an exposure has occurred or controls are not in place; the equipment or operators are not suitable; porous material is in question; hidden microbial contamination is suspected; a waste route is not yet known; or a party asks for a dry, hygienic or occupancy statement. A stop-work decision is correct. Record it, and restart only after the competent party has confirmed the scope in writing.
